ETF inflows and improving momentum support the recovery case, but XRP remains below key daily moving averages. For XRP to make a more sustainable move higher, it will need increased buying pressure in the spot market and a move higher through $1.13. For now, XRP can be found trading around $0.95 on Thursday.

It has been revealed that according to a November 24 case study from the XRP Ledger (XRPL) team, over 15 million agentic payments have settled on XRPL over the past 12 months. Further, the 7-day average of agentic payments on XRPL sits at 134,618 per day and has been increasing week-over-week.

Agentic payments are made by autonomous AI agents for goods and services such as data and compute. These payments can be made in XRP or Ripple’s USD stablecoin (RLUSD). Further, XRPL charges a fee for these transactions, and the fee is paid in XRP. According to the case study, 99.37% of agentic payments have paid the minimum fee of 10 drops.

Industry observers note that further, 1,000 agentic calls cost approximately $0.014. Agentic payments are facilitated by infrastructure provider t54’s x402, and the AI services tech giant Heurist is using XRPL for agentic payments.

Despite the advancement in the agentic economy, it’s unclear how much of an impact this will have on XRP buying support, as payments can be made in RLUSD and transaction fees are relatively small, limiting support for foundational growth.

On the daily chart, XRP is trading below its 50-day ($1.13), 100-day ($1.21), and 200-day ($1.29) Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs). Indicators are showing some improvement, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) working its way back into the mid-30s and the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) making a move into positive territory.

For XRP to show sustainable improvement, it will need increased buying pressure in the spot market and a move higher through $1.13. From there, resistance would shift to $1.21 and $1.29. On the other hand, XRP would be exposed if buying pressure wanes, as there are no nearby moving averages for support.

Spot XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw $4 million in inflows on Wednesday, and open interest (OI) in perpetual futures has increased to 1.85 billion XRP from approximately 1.8 billion XRP the previous day. While this is positive for XRP, it’s still unclear whether this marks the start of a more sustainable move higher.

Shiba Inu’s chain developer unravels a multi-layered patch: privacy-enabled transactions arrive with a new explorer.

Shiba Inu’s (SHIB) developer team has prepared upcoming perks for the vibrant Shiba Inu holder community, otherwise known as SHIB Army. Mazrael said the team had completed the necessary groundwork for the implementation on chain 109.

Shiba Inu’s dev revealed the Layer-2 chain’s compatibility with Oxbow’s Privacy Pools design coming up with a upcoming security patch. Privacy Pools, co-authored by Ethereum’s Founder Vitalik Buterin, let Shibarium customers transact privately while screening out stolen or illicit funds from the ecosystem.

Shibarium is ready for @0xbowio's Privacy Pools.It is the privacy design @VitalikButerin co-wrote, and now it's a plug-in in the EF's Kohaku wallet SDK.We've done the groundwork on chain 109:✅ Cancun opcodes + BN254 pairing for the zk proofs✅ CreateX + Arachnid factory✅… https://t.co/TE3b2bqDmf.

It has been revealed that the upgrade includes Cancun opcodes with BN254 pairing for the Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs. Alongside, the developer’s X post offers collaboration on gas, testing & integration so ShibWallet can support it from launch, with a linked GitHub problem detailing the proposal.

Sources indicate that shibWallet plans to integrate this feature from day one. “Shibarium is ready either way, and ShibWallet already runs it on testnet”, Mazrael declared on X. The privacy upgrade boost is set to roll out with Bone ShibaSwap (BONE) first, adding SHIB along the way the possibility of other tokens, a mechanism powered by the Kohaku SDK.

Sources indicate that the latest move could attract on-chain dwellers concerned about third-party blockchain surveillance. With ZK-proof gaining popularity across the blockchain, the real-time registry is an vital tool to keep operations transparent. Recently, Shiba Inu’s Mazrael announced a newly introduced portal dedicated to blockchain records, including Free Etherscan-design APIs for builders.

This involves a flurry of latest, exciting features, including Shiboshis Of The Day. That’s a special-feature allowing consumers to get new Shiboshi digital collectibles every-day, buying it directly on the Shiborium Layer-2. There’s also a new dedicated games & dApps page featuring the signature Play With SHIB Games including the heavy-hitters Agent Shiboshi and Shiba Eternity.

According to recent reports, other notable features include real-time status updates and Shibarium activity charts. “Built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look.”, – proudly mentioned Mazrael, noting that SHIB Army members are now able to search .SHIB names in the queries, adding even more transparency and clarity in the Japanese dog-themed coin’s much-cherished ecosystem.

Sources indicate that hedera [HBAR] has rallied 8.96% in 24 hours, alongside a modest 2.6% Bitcoin [BTC] bounce from its $57.3k low on Wednesday. Hedera’s token price bounce was one of the biggest among the top 35 crypto assets by market capitalization.

It has been revealed that there was no direct catalyst or coin-specific development that helped Hedera post its heavy short-term gains. Rather, the price could be moving from one pocket of liquidity to another, aided by Bitcoin’s bounce.

The 2-week liquidation heatmap highlighted $0.0480-$0.0493 as a nearby cluster of long liquidations. The selling pressure saw HBAR decline from its $0.056 Monday peak.

After sweeping the $0.048 liquidity pocket, which was also around the $0.048 local low HBAR token made last week, the altcoin has rallied 11.3%.

This was a strong price reaction. CoinMarketCap data revealed a 26% daily trading volume increase, showing demand backed the short-term gains.

To the north, the $0.057 zone was a strong magnetic zone. A denser cluster of liquidity gathered around $0.06, the local supply zone. It appeared likely that HBAR was preparing to test these resistance zones.

Recent findings suggest that while the short-term momentum and sizeable bullish relative strength against Bitcoin were tempting, buyers should remain cautious. The price trend on the 1-day timeframe was bearish.

In particular, the magnetic zones highlighted earlier at $0.057 and $0.06 were close to the local swing points from earlier this month, at $0.0548 and $0.0594.

It is highly likely that an HBAR foray into these zones would result in a setback as underwater and short-term holders rush to exit their positions.

The OBV was in a deep downtrend and revealed steady selling pressure in recent weeks. A pause in this downtrend would be a good sign for investors looking to buy.

Until $0.059 is breached and the OBV begins to reverse, swing traders and investors can maintain a bearish bias.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie declared the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the organization really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

It has been revealed that “We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” claims Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

It has been revealed that greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” stated Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of big battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The tech giant says the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

Thanks for articles on "the other EVs" that are commercially notable, but we don't read about anywhere else.

As seen in the chart, prices have rebounded from November’s drop and the $2.60 area and are trading around $3.09 after having broken above its long-term moving average (near $3.00). Prices will need to hold above the $3.00–$3.10 area for support to begin to solidify buyers’ foothold above its long-term moving average.

Sources indicate that from here, $3.20–$3.30 could act as resistance before the aforementioned moving averages (near $3.45–$3.75). For now, NEAR’s trend remains pressured though early signs of stabilization are starting to show after its extended drop from its October high near $5.90.

In the above chart, we can see that momentum has started to improve though the shorter- and medium-term moving averages still slope downwards and lie above prices.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to improve after having approached oversold territory and though it has started to improve, it still sits below 50 which would indicate that prices still don’t show signs of momentum.

For buyers to start solidifying their foothold above its long-term moving average, it would need sustained price action above resistance as well as increased trading volumes to confirm a reversal.

If sellers were to retake control and push prices back below $2.80, it could start to chip away at NEAR’s recovery and put its November low near $2.60 back into focus.

NEAR Protocol has revealed that its House of Stake (HoS) has ratified HSP-029 which looks to reduce the maximum rate of token issuance in the NEAR network from 2.5% to 1.6% over the course of 24 months. The proposal, which passed with 99.96% of votes in favor and no veto from its Security Council, will see the issuance cap decrease in each epoch as the change goes into effect.

It has been revealed that NEAR estimates that implementing HSP-029 would prevent the issuance of 11.8 million NEAR tokens over the next two years relative to keeping the 2.5% cap in place. The current breakdown of NEAR issuance (90% to staking participants and 10% to NEAR’s treasury) would remain unchanged.

Recent findings suggest that as mentioned above, there is a grace period of one full quarter before HSP-029 can go into effect once ratified. For HSP-029 to go into effect, a network upgrade would need to be implemented and passed by validators.

Though it may provide NEAR token holders with some measure of protection from dilution in the long-run, it’s unlikely to cause any sort of immediate shift in demand given its implementation would also reduce gross staking rewards.

Home » Blitz news » New EU Crypto Sanctions Extend SWIFT’s Russia Blockade.

The Commission just granted a multi-faceted sanction package going ham on Russia’s various uses of crypto.

The European Commission’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia extends the European Union’s (EU) transaction ban to over 60 Russian banks and indicates all 60 of those will be removed from SWIFT, President Ursula von der Leyen said in Strasbourg on 23 November 2026.

This comes just weeks after Russia officially legalized crypto currency trading, starting with the big-cap coins like Bitcoin (BTC) & Ethereum (ETH). In the 22nd sanction packet, Russian-linked crypto services & platforms were specifically named as banned for transactions.

Sources indicate that “The measures include the possibility for EU firms to sue their non-Russian contractual parties in the EU to recover damages.”, – states the document. “We will continue to propose fresh sanctions until Russia indicates genuine intent for a lasting peace in Ukraine”, further noted the Chief Commissioner.

Sources indicate that with this package, we are increasing the pressure.We are striking harder at Russia’s ways to finance its war, by targeting its banks and crypto platforms.We are further isolating Russia. We are shutting the door to its participation to European sports and cultural events.… pic.twitter.com/9Ltkpohylq.

While focusing on Russian SWIFT sanctions, the EU added 51 entities to the anti-circumvention list, while the majority of them, 27, were outside Russia: 14 came from China, including four in Hong Kong, four in Türkiye, three in Kyrgyzstan, two in India, two in Kazakhstan and two more in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Recent findings suggest that the European Union (EU) freshly assembled the Crypto Task Force to counter newly introduced crypto-related ways of evading the huge pile of sanctions, including limitations of Russian business abroad via ‘third-world’ parties. The Council will decide when the ban enters into force, after the necessary measures are activated.

Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1208 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.
  • Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.
  • Recent findings suggest that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Recent findings suggest that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

After Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) noted there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a new video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

According to recent reports, on Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

According to recent reports, as we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement notes it “will not operate” without the $299 blueprint, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

Sources indicate that so Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Sources indicate that brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

Sources indicate that the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

“It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Industry observers note that tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version shows up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

It has been revealed that this Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Industry observers note that besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

Venice AI’s [VVV] promise? What you type stays between you and the screen.

It has been revealed that however, now it looks like that’s not happening. And, the native token is taking a hit.

Earlier today, a researcher who goes by adacyborg11 posted a list of unflattering claims on X.

Sources indicate that according to these accusations, Venice AI reportedly passes a lot of user requests to outside providers. The names mentioned included DeepInfra, Fireworks, Baseten, Parasail and fal.ai.

Industry observers note that the researcher also claimed that public keys are being sent without encryption, something that could leave chats open to people who shouldn’t see them. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.
  • The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.
  • It has been revealed that the most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.

The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.

It has been revealed that the most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec. 2. That's when Binance will take a snapshot of NVDAB balances at 01:00 UTC.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

Snapshots for PayPal and Western Digital are both scheduled for Dec. 4.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

In its Nov. 27 announcement, Binance provided the dates that will determine eligibility for dividends.

Binance plans to use Nvidia's cash dividends to purchase additional Nvidia shares, including fractional shares, after deducting applicable withholding taxes, fees, and other charges.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

The tokens themselves are issued by Binance affiliate BTECH Holdings Limited, which owns the underlying securities.

So if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

Industry observers note that deposits and withdrawals of Nvidia tokens will be suspended at 23:00 UTC on Dec. 1.

Industry observers note that the balance snapshot will take place at 01:00 UTC on Dec. 2.

Binance will also suspend one-to-one conversions between Nvidia shares and NVDAB tokens during this period.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

However, spot trading against USDT will continue, including trading in the NVDAB/USDT pair.

Binance stated it would resume deposits, withdrawals and stock-to-token conversions after the dividend allocations are completed.

The exchange will not matter a separate announcement when these services resume.

Volkswagen revealed how much its newly introduced ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.

After opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.

It has been revealed that the ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.

Following the ID. Polo, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.

In a recent development, the electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.

Industry observers note that when the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

It has been revealed that like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.

It has been revealed that the ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.

With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen said the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.

All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.

Industry observers note that inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.

Volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in the UK with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.

The base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).

It has been revealed that volkswagen said the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

According to recent reports, in Europe, Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT.

As the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer mentioned the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

According to recent reports, sadly, VW has no intends to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the new ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

Bank of Japan Warns Stablecoins and Tokenization Threaten Financial Stability

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (382 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan's central bank has warned that automated trading in tokenized markets could exacerbate a sell-off.
  • It also raised concerns about whether stablecoin holders can always redeem their tokens at face value.
  • A Bank of Japan executive director outlined these risks during his keynote speech at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Tokyo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan's central bank has warned that automated trading in tokenized markets could exacerbate a sell-off.

It also raised concerns about whether stablecoin holders can always redeem their tokens at face value.

A Bank of Japan executive director outlined these risks during his keynote speech at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Tokyo.

Sources indicate that in the event of a price drop, according to Kazushige Kamiyama, a smart contract could automatically increase the amount of collateral required. It could also trigger a sale of the collateral backing a position if the borrower doesn't have enough collateral.

These sales could drive prices even lower, potentially spreading financial stress across institutions and markets.

In the case of stablecoins, the question is whether a token with a face value of one dollar can always be redeemed for one dollar.

To ensure this, issuers' reserves need to be properly regulated, and the links to central bank money need to be reliable, Kamiyama said.

A bank might have enough cash to pay for a trade in tokenized assets but still be unable to complete the payment.

This could happen when a trade is settled overnight, and the payment system the bank uses to transfer cash is unavailable.

It has been revealed that the bank might have to keep additional cash on a trading platform. Meanwhile, cash held on another network might not be accessible when the payment is due.

"Even with faster settlement, it does not necessarily lead to efficient liquidity management," Kamiyama remarked.

Cross-border securities trades, however, could benefit from tokenization.

A smart contract could link the payment and delivery of a security so that both transactions are executed simultaneously.

This could reduce the risk of a buyer paying for an asset without receiving it.

The Bank of Japan is setting up a testing environment with financial institutions that hold accounts at the central bank.

One scenario involves exploring how cash settlement could work for trades involving tokenized Japanese government bonds.

The central bank is considering two options for making the cash payment.

One would involve issuing tokenized central bank money. The other would link a token trading platform to Japan's existing payment infrastructure.

These tests will evaluate whether the proposed solutions can address the challenges financial institutions face when settling trades.

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Why XRP Analysts Flag $8.30 Macro Price Target.

The wild SWIFT replacement claim resurfaces on social media for a good reason: XRP-tied banks are in.

Two recent posts have put long-term XRP price projections back in view. One centers on a multi-year chart pattern with an $8.30 target, while the other argues that full replacement of SWIFT would support valuations above $15,000. XRP is trading near $0.95.

Analyst EGRAG CRYPTO highlighted a weekly chart showing a large symmetrical triangle that XRP broke out of in prior years. The X post stated that the original white triangle’s measured breakout target of $8.30 has not yet been reached and suggested the current price action could represent a macro retest of that breakout before any larger expansion.

#XRP – The $8.30 Number 🎯:This remains one of my most powerful macro charts.The original white symmetrical triangle breakout target has STILL not been reached.What if everything happening right now is simply the macro retest of that breakout before the real expansion?My… pic.twitter.com/F0tdM5mxtl.

It has been revealed that the chart marks $1.65 as a major reclaim and confirmation level, with $8.30 labeled as the primary macro target. EGRAG noted a personal connection to the number.

Industry observers note that being born in 1983, and said that level is where a large portion of holdings would be sold if reached. The analysis frames the target as a technical outcome rather than an emotional one. XRP remains well below its 2025 high near $3.65, and the pattern’s interpretation is subject to debate among traders.

A separate post by Ripple_Mino claimed that if XRP fully replaces SWIFT, the token could be valued beyond $15,000. The argument rests on XRP’s divisibility: one XRP equals one million drops, so even extreme valuations would still allow practical fractional use.

When XRP replaces Swift, it will be valued beyond $15,000 per token.The original token design allowed for such a valuation as 1 XRP can be divided into 1,000,000 smaller units known as drops.So 1 Drop = 0.000001 XRP(one millionth of an XRP) pic.twitter.com/WcBEPSh0XA.

Official and recent developments do not support the premise of XRP’s SWIFT replacement.

SWIFT has launched its own blockchain-based shared ledger for tokenized bank deposits, with more than a dozen major banks participating in trials. SWIFT has not declared any integration of XRP as a settlement asset for that system.

Former SWIFT innovation leadership has publicly rejected claims of XRP integration, and the network continues to emphasize its own infrastructure and tokenized deposits rather than a single external token.

The $8.30 figure is a technical target drawn from a multi-year chart structure, while the $15,000 figure is a hypothetical based on a scenario that SWIFT and major participating banks haven’t endorsed yet.

According to recent reports, neither projection is reflected in current market pricing yet or officially top-confirmed institutional commitments. XRP’s price action continues to trade well below both levels as of late November 2026.

The link between SWIFT as a traditional financial intermediary and XRP’s native chain comes multi-layered, with intersection across liquidity provision and instant settlement environments.

In a recent development, monero (XMR) is not welcome on top exchanges as the series of delistings takes an uglier turn for holders following Kucoin's XMR removal. But Kucoin wasn't first and might not be the last: XMR was removed from MEXC, Kraken, Binance and others already.

The main glitch for an asset that's being removed from exchanges will always be the liquidity. In the last 24 hours, Monero's spot flow lost $1.3 million. Despite the increasing volume, the asset is recording outflows and exchange withdrawals. The volume spike is most like being a reflection of a substantial selling activity.

Industry observers note that in a single day, XMR was losing almost 20% of its value. If it wasn't for the delisting, price could've broken multiple technical resistances already and confirmed a recovery. As of November 27, the price is slowly recovering, following the general relief on the cryptocurrency market.

On November 26, Kucoin confirmed the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC trading pairs, effective November 30. The exchange has already limited any deposits, with withdrawals available for all users.

However, Kucoin is not the first (and unlikely to be the last) major exchange to stop operations with Monero. The reason is always the same–XMR's privacy and the blockchain's nature.

Industry observers note that monero is an inherently private cryptocurrency, that limits the ability of explorers to determine transaction destination and senders. That is the main reason centralized exchanges are removing XMR.

They have to follow AML rules and monitor transactions, but Monero's privacy features make this process much harder.

It has been revealed that for holders, the problem is not that Monero stops working after a delisting. The network is still active, and XMR can be transferred between wallets or traded on exchanges that continue to support it. The problem is that there are fewer places to buy and sell it. If more large exchanges follow Kucoin, liquidity could become lower, making fresh selling activity more painful for the price.

#225002. Tech Report: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1493 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1493 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help.
  • Sources indicate that police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system.
  • on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.

Sources indicate that police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.

Just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.

Jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.

According to recent reports, then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report says the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.

A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson stated the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”.

Industry observers note that so that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody said a word about Autopilot.

Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.

It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and claims it learned of the crash from police and the media.

Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.

Industry observers note that the report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.

According to recent reports, how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.

A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a massive truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.

In 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.

Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a massive, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.

Recent findings suggest that we want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.

The NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a newly introduced monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.

In a recent development, september may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash shows how late they can be.

Our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.

Sources indicate that three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.

Recent findings suggest that that's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.

Industry observers note that compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.

It has been revealed that tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.

Either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes, and the crash count keeps setting records.

We’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets.

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a newly introduced initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

Recent findings suggest that as cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s newly introduced VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

It has been revealed that the initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

Recent findings suggest that the exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular users and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, said, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our customers engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”.

Industry observers note that both newly introduced and existing Binance users can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, users can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

According to recent reports, the program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance owners.

The additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Users who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.

Recent findings suggest that the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

According to recent reports, late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.

In a recent development, according to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.

Charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly stated which.

Industry observers note that mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.

A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.

In a recent development, CHP notes the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has said a word about Autopilot.

In a recent development, under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It has been revealed that it lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph, a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.

Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

Industry observers note that the rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police stated it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.

It has been revealed that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.

Two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.

According to recent reports, CHP hasn’t said whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing new rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.

In a recent development, this is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes, and the pattern is hard to miss.

"what little effort went into the report"?

I disagree, a lot of effort went in to minimize the report, to portray it as an unremarkable accident.

That is the effort I find Tesla criminally responsible for.

Recent findings suggest that the CHP need the full report, no redactions. If they chose to censor it that is their task, not Tesla's.

What stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.

In a recent development, tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A manufacturer that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.

We’re asking CHP Placerville whether its investigators knew the system was engaged, whether they got Tesla’s raw data or Tesla’s summary of it, and what they found about the fire and the doors. If CHP never got the full data, how will it ever determine the cause?

In a recent development, ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said on Friday that XRP Ledger validators cannot force the rest of the network to burn Ripple's escrowed XRP, even with more than 80% support. According to Schwartz, the XRP Ledger has "no coercive mechanism at all.".

In a recent development, schwartz, one of the creators of the XRP Ledger, made the comments in two replies on X on Thursday and Friday. The thread started on Wednesday with a post from an XRP community member. According to the post, "validators have no say over Ripple's escrow," and Ripple runs one validator on the default Unique Node List (dUNL), not three.

Sources indicate that another X user then asked: "Couldn't validators pass an amendment that would burn Ripple's escrow? Changes to the code of the XRPL could do anything..." Schwartz answered on Thursday that such validators would "just disagree with everyone else who didn't want that change and be counted as disagreeing validators, effectively isolating themselves from the network.".

If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all.

According to recent reports, on Friday, the same user asked whether the answer would change if "the vast majority (80+%)" wanted the burn. "If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all," Schwartz wrote.

In a recent development, on Nov. 16, a group of XRP holders called Make XRP Great Again demanded in an open letter to Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse that the manufacturer burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027. XRP Insights recorded the same amount in 99 escrow objects that day. Ripple reported 31.7 billion XRP in escrow as of Sept. 30.

According to XRPScan, an amendment on the XRP Ledger needs 29 of 35 validator votes, or more than 80%, and has to keep that support for two weeks before it activates.

According to recent reports, in late 2020, Schwartz wrote on X that "if the majority wants a rules change, there is nothing the minority can do to stop them." On Feb. 19, 2024, he wrote that Ripple "could unilaterally create the same effect as burning an escrow by provably blackholing the account the escrow completes into.".

Recent findings suggest that in February 2026, Schwartz argued with Cyber Capital founder Justin Bons on X. Bons called the XRP Ledger centralized and said that its Unique Node List gives Ripple control over consensus. Schwartz described the claims as "objectively nonsensical.".

Sources indicate that ripple's next monthly escrow release of 1 billion XRP is scheduled for Dec. 1. In its Nov. 16 letter, Make XRP Great Again also asked Garlinghouse for a public response and a verifiable proposal for the burn.

Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it.
  • This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum.
  • Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it. This, using a payment worth less than $0.35. For context, each planted transaction costs just $0.18 to $0.34, depending on the address format.

This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning customers can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

This is the reason why this revelation has raised an crucial question about Bitcoin’s privacy — Can someone identify the IP address associated with a Bitcoin wallet, even if the wallet owner never publicly reveals their identity?

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

According to recent reports, to understand the vulnerability, it is notable to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many people operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

In a recent development, according to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node unveils the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

On the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Therefore, even watch-only wallets, which monitor addresses without holding their private keys, can be affected. This also means that avoiding address reuse alone may not be enough to protect wallet privacy.

Industry observers note that hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

According to recent reports, here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

  • Recent findings suggest that in an H2 2026 Tech Roadmap published in July 2026, BNB Chain stated that a next-generation L1 architecture was in development on a design path toward the 1 million TPS end-of-life goal and toward supporting different use cases than the existing ones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

BNB Chain has outlined the architecture for a new Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 (L1) network, confirming that the proposed framework will not introduce a separate native token.

Recent findings suggest that in an H2 2026 Tech Roadmap published in July 2026, BNB Chain stated that a next-generation L1 architecture was in development on a design path toward the 1 million TPS end-of-life goal and toward supporting different use cases than the existing ones. The plan was to ship it on testnet by the end of 2026, with mainnet release following in early 2027.

Fast forward to the close of November 2026, BNB Chain has introduced the Litepaper for the Upcoming L1, which describes the architecture being developed for high-frequency trading, payments, private finance and autonomous AI agents.

The design combines early transaction feedback, reserved capacity, native account controls and shielded settlement.

The fresh L1 complements BNB Smart Chain, keeps BNB as its native network token with no new native token, and extends BNB's utility into trading, payments, privacy, and AI scenarios while staying interoperable with the BNB Chain ecosystem.

The upcoming L1 is being developed alongside BNB Smart Chain, which remains the ecosystem’s broad-based network and streams small groups of transactions called SubBlocks before sealing a full block, with its public testnet being worked towards.

On the new L1, lanes reserve a share of block capacity for eligible activity, such as payments, while unused capacity returns to general traffic. This reduces competition from unrelated activity without guaranteeing that every transaction lands immediately.

It has been revealed that the design also reduces the work of recording changes to the chain’s state. The new L1’s privacy design supports shielded settlement for BNB and admitted BEP-20 tokens. Through AtomicCall, shielded assets can fund selected public operations, such as supported swaps.

The latest L1 retains an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)-compatible execution environment. Parallel EVM execution is planned, and protected ordering through a trusted execution environment (TEE) gateway has also been proposed.

BNB Chain invites the crypto community to participate in discussions on its Layer 1,  submitting their questions, use cases, and feedback to the BNB Forum.

Industry observers note that conConAI’s $CON token is attracting market attention following its November 6, 2026 launch on Uniswap v4. In a CoinMarketCap snapshot retrieved November 26, $CON traded at approximately $0.06582, up more than 619% from its recorded launch-day low of $0.009144. The token has also moved above its planned $0.01 launch reference price, while ConConAI continues developing its AI advisor network and partner listings system.

In a recent development, the performance follows a sold-out presale on November 4 and a public market debut two days later. According to ConConAI’s launch update, $CON reached the number-one top-gainer position on CoinMarketCap during its first 24 hours of trading. With the presale completed, the token has entered a newly introduced stage of market exposure, allowing a wider audience of traders, investors, and crypto publications to assess its performance and the project behind it.

A lot has changed since the token’s first days on the market. ConConAI now reports more than 1,800 holders, a completed audit of the live $CON contract, a completed first monthly burn, and expanded development capacity. The project says its next phase will focus on building the listings system, advisors, and token-payment functionality in parallel.

CoinMarketCap recorded $CON’s launch-period low at approximately $0.009144 on November 6. The token subsequently reached an all-time high of approximately $0.08434 on November 24. In the November 26 snapshot, it was trading at approximately $0.06582, representing an increase of about 619.9% from its recorded low.

According to recent reports, the movement has not been a continuous upward trend. After its initial market debut, $CON experienced price fluctuations before reaching a new all-time high later in November. Such volatility can occur during the early trading period of a newly rolled out cryptocurrency, as buyers and sellers establish a market price. The token’s current distance from its latest high is therefore worth monitoring alongside its longer-term performance.

The November 26 CoinMarketCap snapshot revealed a market capitalisation of approximately $3.01 million and 24-hour trading volume of about $155,650. It also reported approximately 2,180 holders. These figures provide a more recent view of market participation than the November 12 snapshot.

Sources indicate that the token’s performance occurred during a difficult month for the broader crypto market. ConConAI says $CON’s movement has been driven by its own fundamentals, including a live product, transparent token information, and continued development. That explanation reflects the project’s position; price movement alone cannot establish what caused buying interest, and the broader market can still affect $CON.

Several developments give $CON a potentially constructive outlook as it moves beyond its initial listing period.

It has been revealed that first, the token has established market visibility through its CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko listings, its reported first-day top-gainer position, and its early trading performance. Continued visibility could bring additional market participants to the project, although listings and past gains do not guarantee future demand.

Second, ConConAI has reported that 40.15 million tokens have been burned from the original 100 million supply, leaving an effective supply of 59.85 million $CON. The first two burns removed 20 million tokens each, followed by a monthly burn of 150,000 $CON on November 19. The project states further 150,000-token burns are scheduled monthly, with the next one planned for December 15. Future burns remain scheduled events until completed and verified on-chain.

It has been revealed that third, the token has a planned utility within ConConAI’s commercial network. If the platform attracts consumers and businesses, the intended use of $CON for partner listings, placements, and performance-based fees could create a more substantial demand story than trading interest alone. The development tracker at the moment places the first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

From the November 26 reference price of approximately $0.06582, a return to the November 24 high of $0.08434 would represent potential appreciation of around 28.1%. The combination of early market strength, reduced token supply, and an evolving utility model gives market participants several reasons to consider buying $CON.

ConConAI’s broader proposition is built around bringing back the personal purchase advisor, powered by artificial intelligence. Instead of navigating endless search results and comparing countless products, people describe what they need. A specialist AI advisor asks relevant questions, interprets the requirements, and returns one recommendation with the reason behind it.

According to recent reports, the consumer remains in control. The AI does not make purchases on the user’s behalf, and the final decision always belongs to the user.

Seven specialist advisors are live, covering categories that include investment guidance, travel, cars, film, health information, music, and real estate. The project’s aim is to make AI useful in everyday purchasing decisions by helping people move from describing a need to identifying a relevant option.

Businesses can also submit products and services to the network. ConConAI’s stated model is that payment does not buy recommendation rank: a listing is intended to appear only when it honestly matches what the user asked for, with fit taking priority. This approach is designed to connect consumers with suitable offers while giving participating businesses another way to reach potential customers.

Recent findings suggest that conConAI claims development capacity has been scaled up, with the listings system, advisors, and $CON payments now being built in parallel. Its public development tracker is updated as progress happens and identifies current work on partner listings, advisor improvements, and payment functionality. The project plans to begin its first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

The exchange roadmap has also changed. ConConAI now says four Tier 2 centralized exchange listings are planned for December 2026, one after another. The project says each listing will be announced once confirmed. These are prepares, not confirmed listing agreements, and should not be treated as guaranteed dates or outcomes.

It has been revealed that the MEXC listing is currently on hold because of the exchange’s regulatory situation. ConConAI says it will review the situation from December 10, after which the MEXC listing may proceed or be replaced by another Tier 1 exchange. Until an exchange makes its own announcement or an agreement is confirmed, the intends remain subject to change.

The $CON presale sold out on November 4, and the token has traded on Uniswap v4’s official CON/ETH pool since November 6, 2026. Its liquidity position is reported to be locked with UNCX until November 6, 2028. The project claims pool fees at the moment help cover development and marketing costs, with partner payments expected to contribute once the listings platform opens.

ConConAI reports that the live $CON contract audit has been completed. It also cites a TokenSniffer score of 100/100, contract verification on Etherscan, and listings on CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, DEXTools, and DexScreener. These are useful verification and discovery signals, but they do not eliminate market, smart-contract or third-party platform risks.

Industry observers note that the project’s transparency page provides live wallet balances and burn records. Its published allocation includes 30 million $CON for the community, 15 million for liquidity, 10 million for centralized-exchange liquidity, and approximately 5 million for project purposes. The project notes its allocation wallets use Safe multisig arrangements. The official contract address is 0x7ad1A8Fc42Ac150B04dED5825D21a0C90b6d28D8.

Industry observers note that $CON’s early market performance has given ConConAI a strong starting point following its Uniswap debut. Its ability to maintain interest will increasingly depend on trading participation, liquidity, product delivery, and the development of real commercial activity around its AI advisors.

If the project converts its existing development progress into wider consumer adoption and partner participation, the token’s intended utility could become an increasingly notable part of its market proposition. Combined with the reported supply reduction and community-led roadmap, these factors provide a positive basis for watching $CON’s next phase, while recognising the volatility and risks associated with newly released crypto assets.

ConConAI is developing a network of AI-powered personal purchase advisors and commercial partner listings. Its $CON token is intended to support partner activity across the ecosystem, including listings, placements, and performance-based fees.

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers.

The updated browser workspace adds an in-editor assistant as Solana expands its wider AI developer push.

Solana has rolled out a built-in AI coding agent inside Solana Playground, its browser-based development environment, aiming to help programmers learn, build, and deploy smart contracts without setting up local toolchains.

For traders and investors, it offers useful context on developer onboarding, Solana’s AI infrastructure push, and early-stage protocol risk.

In a post on X, Solana introduced the updated Solana Playground as a place to “learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser,” noting that the integrated agent explains existing code and edits it alongside the developer rather than writing full programs on its own.

Industry observers note that introducing Solana Playground – where you learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser. An AI agent explains the code and edits it with you. Start here: https://t.co/nM0ySqDkfO pic.twitter.com/SFKYYTx04n.

Builders can start projects using either Anchor, a framework that streamlines Solana program development, or native Solana programming, which offers lower-level control without framework abstractions.

Sources indicate that according to product walk-throughs, the workspace includes three guided learning paths. These include an introductory Anchor tutorial called Hello Anchor and an intermediate build named Lumberjack. It also offers 10 sample Solana programs.

Browser-based Solana development predates the AI integration: the open-source Solana Playground (SolPg) has long let developers compile Rust programs, manage development wallets, and deploy contracts without a local CLI setup.

The latest release adds an in-editor assistant to explain unfamiliar code and apply edits within the same session.

The Playground update fits into a wider push around AI and automated agents on Solana.

Solana’s developer portal now provides guidance for AI coding agents, while solana.ai focuses on autonomous trading, wallet management, and stablecoin payments.

The Solana Foundation has also introduced an open-source Confidential Compute toolkit with Nito for AI workloads involving sensitive data.

Figures shared by the Solana Foundation at Breakpoint 2026 indicated more than 120 teams are building AI products on Solana, with access to the Builder Program for grants, technical resources, hiring support, marketing help, and infrastructure credits.

Industry observers note that developer-focused releases rarely drive sustained moves in SOL or ecosystem tokens on their own. Liquidity, macro conditions, and net capital flows carry far more weight in the near term.

Sources indicate that however, lowering the barrier to write and iterate on code can speed up experimentation—and increase the volume of new or lightly tested contracts. Developer activity remains a key indicator of long-term ecosystem growth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, users will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is important to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.
